title: frame_length cast to u8 without range validation on RX path
description:
**File:** rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs
**Line:** 632

**Issue:** The frame_length is computed as usize (4 + dst_addr.len() + inner_payload.len() + SIGNATURE_LENGTH) and then cast to u8 in the verify_frame call. If frame_length > 255, this silently truncates.

On the TX path (line 589), there's a check at line 590 against MAX_FRAME_BODY before the cast. On the RX path, no such validation occurs before line 632's cast.

**Trigger:** Receiving a malformed frame claiming addr/payload lengths that sum to > 255 bytes. The truncated frame_length would be passed to verify_frame, potentially causing signature verification against wrong data.

**Bad behavior:** Signature verification uses truncated length, could accept invalid signature or reject valid one.

**Suggested fix:** Add explicit range check: 'if frame_length > MAX_FRAME_BODY { return Err(...); }' before the cast, or use TryFrom<usize>::try_into() to make truncation explicit.
close_reason: Added rx_frame_length(dst_len,payload_len) helper in link_layer.rs: checked arithmetic + explicit MAX_FRAME_BODY range validation before the u8 cast on the RX path; oversize/overflow now returns FrameError::FrameTooLarge instead of truncating signature input. Tests: boundary Ok(254), one-over rejected, usize::MAX overflow-safe, end-to-end jumbo-wire rejection via receive_frame.
